title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Part 1 (end of the computation from p.7). Grothendieck wants the explicit conformal isomorphism g from the unit disk D onto the single open face f of the 'monogone' map on P^1(C). This map has one edge [0,1], vertex 0, and face centre ∞. The prescribed values are g(0)=∞, g(1)=0, g(-1)=1, g(±i)=1/2 on the two banks of the cut.

He obtains g from a degree-2 covering X_1 → X_0 = P^1. On X_1 = P^1 the vertex is 1, the edge is the unit circle, the face centres are 0 and ∞, and the edge midpoint is -1. The covering is required to send 1 ↦ 0, -1 ↦ 1 and {0,∞} ↦ ∞. He conjugates the model map g'(z)=z^2 by Möbius maps:
- ψ(z) = (z-1)/(z+1) sends 1 ↦ 0, -1 ↦ ∞, {0,∞} ↦ {-1,1}.
- φ(z) = σ_0(z) = z/(z-1) sends 0 ↦ 0, ∞ ↦ 1, 1 ↦ ∞.

So g = φ∘g'∘ψ = w^2/(w^2-1) with w = ψ(z). This simplifies to (z-1)^2/((z-1)^2-(z+1)^2) = -(z-1)^2/(4z), formula (23). In modern terms, -(z-1)^2/(4z) = (1 - J(z))/2 with J(z) = (z+1/z)/2 the Joukowski map. J sends D conformally onto P^1 minus [-1,1], and the affine map t ↦ (1-t)/2 sends [-1,1] onto [0,1]. Hence g sends D onto P^1 minus [0,1], with g(1)=0, g(-1)=1, g(±i)=1/2 and g(0)=∞, as announced. This is the explicit uniformisation of a face of a map by the standard disk, as used when building the Riemann surface of a map by gluing standard polygons.

Part 2. Here τ is complex conjugation on U_{0,3} = P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. Grothendieck identifies the extended group Π_{0,3}^τ with a 'mixed' fundamental group π_1(U_{0,3},{1,τ}; P_+), i.e. the fundamental group of U_{0,3} equipped with the action of {1,τ} (orbifold/equivariant π_1, a semidirect product π_1(U) ⋊ Z/2). The base point P_+ is the pole of the upper half-plane, and P_- = τP_+.

The Q_i are the midpoints of the three real arcs, each opposite the puncture i: Q_1 = -1, Q_0 = 2, Q_∞ = 1/2. The λ_i are paths from P_- to P_+ through Q_i along great half-circles. The pairs τ_i = (λ_i, τ) are elements of the mixed group. They are involutions, namely the reflections in the three sides of the ideal triangle. The marginal NB ρ_i = λ_{i+1}λ_{i-1}^{-1} expresses the loops around the punctures as products of two of these.

Thus Π_{0,3}^τ ≅ Z/2 * Z/2 * Z/2, the extended (∞,∞,∞) triangle group, containing the free group π_1(U_{0,3}) with index 2. The next page uses this: (possibly non-oriented) weighted maps correspond to {1,τ}-coverings of U_{0,3} in which the τ_i act without fixed points. That is, X'^τ = ∅, where X' is the orientation double cover of the map and τ is the deck involution reversing orientation.
errors: In the first expression for g the denominator is written (w)^2 + 1 instead of w^2 - 1 (since φ(u) = u/(u-1)). The next step, (z-1)^2/((z-1)^2-(z+1)^2), silently uses the correct sign, so the final formula (23) g(z) = -(z-1)^2/(4z) is correct.
Minor: on p.7 the edge of X_1 is described as the 'equator in P^1(R)'. With faces centred at 0 and ∞, the edge must be the unit circle, which is consistent with g(±i) = 1/2 here.

ideas.what: Explicit conformal map from the unit disk onto P^1 minus [0,1], obtained by Möbius-conjugating z^2
ideas.modern_name: Joukowski map (affinely normalised); conformal uniformisation of a face of a dessin/map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Joukowski (classical); use in dessin theory standard (e.g. Jones–Singerman)

ideas.what: Extended group Π_{0,3}^τ as the fundamental group of U_{0,3} with the complex-conjugation action, with explicit generators τ_i = (path from P_- to P_+ through Q_i, τ)
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant/orbifold fundamental group; π_1 of P^1_R minus {0,1,∞}, i.e. π_1 ⋊ Gal(C/R); extended triangle group Z/2*Z/2*Z/2 generated by reflections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical reflection groups; for maps: Jones–Singerman (1978), Bryant–Singerman (1985); real Belyi theory: Köck–Singerman (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses non-oriented maps and the non-oriented cartographic group; an explicit 'mixed fundamental group' formulation there is unsure

ideas.what: Loops around the punctures as products of the involutions (ρ_i = λ_{i+1}λ_{i-1}^{-1})
ideas.modern_name: Rotation = product of two reflections in the extended triangle group

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, in 1981-82, the dictionary between (non-oriented) maps and {1,τ}-equivariant coverings of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, i.e. real Belyi theory. Fixed points of the reflections τ_i correspond to real components over the arcs, and the absence of boundary corresponds to X'^τ = ∅. This anticipates later work (Bryant–Singerman 1985, Köck–Singerman's real Belyi theory) in an étale/π_1 language. The content is known today, so this is priority/historical interest only.
missed.quote: Le groupe Π_{03}^τ apparaît comme un groupe fondamental mixte (24) Π_{0,3}^τ ≃ π_1(U_{0,3}, {1,τ}; P_+)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the equivariant-π_1 viewpoint on non-orientable dessins / real Belyi theory; no new mathematics for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is a routine Joukowski-type uniformisation with a small sign slip. The mixed fundamental group description of the extended triangle group and its link to non-oriented maps and real curves is a nice early formulation, but it is known in the later literature (Jones–Singerman, Bryant–Singerman, Köck–Singerman) and partly echoed in the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: The image indeed shows '+1' in the denominator of the first expression for g. This is Grothendieck's own slip (it should be -1), not a transcription error; the '[?]' can be removed.
(23) reads g(z) = -(1/(4z))(z-1)^2; the '42' in the image is '4z'.
The marginal note reads roughly 'NB Ici ρ_i = λ_{i+1} λ_{i-1}^{-1}'.
The line under (24) annotates τ as: τP_+ = P_-, with λ_i : P_- → P_+ an arrow in Π_1(U_{0,3},{1,τ}).
